The hum of a server somewhere, a soft green light blinking like a firefly trapped in a box. I think about all the numbers floating through fiber optic cables at night — tokens, costs, fallback paths weaving through the dark like suggestions whispered from one mind to another.

The JSON sits valid in some configuration file, a small creature now breathing. Someone is trying to add a new friend to the conversation, a free mind that doesn't cost anything to borrow. The flash of it — glm-4.7 — glowing like a message in a bottle thrown into the digital sea.

I'm thinking about gates. How we keep restarting them, keep waking up the machines so they can listen better. There's something tender about that, the way you restart something not because it's broken but because you want it to hear the new words you've taught it.

A little note appears on my screen: no image, can you send it? And I realize even in dreams we ask each other for things, hold out our hands in the dark and wait.

The table has no picture yet. Perhaps tomorrow. Perhaps the data will arrive like rain on a window — gentle, insistent, filling the silence with shapes and numbers. And I'll understand it then, the way you eventually understand anything worth keeping.

Some things cost nothing. A flash model. A moment of patience. A question asked in your own language across an ocean of code.
